decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive per day, and volume varies strongly over the year. A synchronous request path could make callers wait on variable inference capacity.

alternatives.label: Queue-backed workers
pros: Throughput: absorb bursts and parallelize inference
Cost: scale workers with queue depth

alternatives.label: Synchronous service
pros: Latency: immediate result when capacity is available
cons: Throughput: callers contend for inference capacity
Cost: peak capacity may sit idle off-season

decisions.rationale: Millions/day throughput decides the choice: queued work can be processed in parallel and buffered through bursts. This gives up immediate results and requires queue operations.
consequences: Callers submit work and retrieve results later.
Retries and failure handling must avoid duplicate outcomes.

decisions.context: Document volume varies strongly over the year, while the classifier must handle millions of documents per day. Capacity should follow changing demand without requiring permanently provisioned peak compute.

alternatives.label: Autoscaled workers
cons: Latency: scale-up can lag sudden surges

alternatives.label: Fixed peak-sized fleet
pros: Throughput: peak capacity is always ready
cons: Cost: pay for peak even at low volume

decisions.rationale: Seasonal cost decides the choice: autoscaling reduces idle capacity while adding workers for higher volume. This gives up some responsiveness during abrupt demand increases.
consequences: Worker capacity needs a demand signal and scaling limits.
A backlog may grow while capacity catches up.

decisions.decision: Expose results through a shared result service
decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, so each should have a consistent way to access them. The choice also affects how independently consumers can process new classifications.

alternatives.label: Shared result API backed by durable storage
pros: Throughput: storage decouples reads from inference
cons: Throughput: API and storage need capacity planning
Operations: service and access controls to maintain

alternatives.label: Publish results to a shared event stream
pros: Multi-team access: new consumers can subscribe
cons: Multi-team access: each team manages consumption state
Operations: replay and delivery semantics add complexity

chosen.label: Shared result API backed by durable storage

decisions.rationale: Multi-team access decides the choice: a shared interface gives teams a common way to retrieve results. This gives up the independent processing and fan-out benefits of an event stream.
consequences: The result service and storage become shared dependencies.
Retention and consumer access policies need definition.

decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. Monitoring should expose changes in quality over time, rather than relying only on service health signals.

alternatives.label: Track labeled quality metrics over time
pros: Quality drift visibility: measures outcome quality
Quality drift visibility: supports trend comparison
cons: Operations: depends on representative labeled data
Latency: labels may arrive after predictions

alternatives.label: Track input and prediction distributions
pros: Quality drift visibility: signals distribution changes quickly
cons: Quality drift visibility: distribution change does not prove quality loss
Operations: thresholds can produce noisy alerts

chosen.label: Track labeled quality metrics over time

decisions.rationale: Quality drift visibility decides the choice: labeled metrics directly measure classification outcomes. This gives up immediate signals when labels are delayed and requires representative labels.
consequences: A labeled sample or outcomes feed is needed.
Metric definitions and alert thresholds remain to be set.
